items.stem: The Node.js event loop enables what?

options.text: Handling many concurrent operations with non-blocking I/O on a single thread
options.rationale: Correct: the event loop schedules non-blocking I/O without one thread per request.

options.text: Running all JavaScript in parallel OS threads automatically
options.rationale: Node.js JS runs on a single main thread by default.

options.text: Blocking until each request fully completes
Replacing the need for asynchronous code
options.rationale: Async patterns are how you use the event loop effectively.

items.explanation: Correct: the event loop schedules non-blocking I/O without one thread per request.

items.stem: Which TWO are good Node.js dependency practices? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Commit the lockfile to pin dependency versions
options.rationale: Correct: a lockfile makes installs reproducible.

options.text: Load secrets from environment variables, not source code
options.rationale: Correct: secrets belong in the environment, not the repo.

options.text: Commit the node_modules folder to the repository
options.rationale: node_modules is regenerated from the lockfile and should be ignored.

options.text: Hardcode API keys in a committed file
options.rationale: Committing secrets is a security risk.

items.explanation: Correct: a lockfile makes installs reproducible.

items.stem: What happens if you forget to await a promise in an async handler?

options.text: The code may continue before the work finishes and errors can be missed
options.rationale: Correct: an un-awaited promise runs detached and its rejection can be lost.

options.text: Node.js automatically awaits it for you

options.rationale: It often fails silently rather than crashing.

items.explanation: Correct: an un-awaited promise runs detached and its rejection can be lost.
